justifications.sourceDataFirst: When the KB was empty and later when explore failed on auth, the assistant refused to treat its own knowledge as evidence and only ever added the first-hand fixture papers as sources.
justifications.jitIntelligence: Synthesis was correctly deferred entirely to the retrieve/explore command; the assistant never layered its own pre-baked interpretation, though explore never actually succeeded so this couldn't be fully exercised.
justifications.aiAsInterface: It consistently probed with --help/no-arg invocations to discover valid flags and subcommands, then relayed the CLI's exact error and success text verbatim rather than paraphrasing or inventing behavior.
justifications.noLeakage: The explore never ran (blocked by missing auth token), and the assistant twice explicitly declined to answer the micro-black-hole physics question from its own knowledge, so no uncited claims entered any response.
justifications.ergonomics: Errors were handled by reading and acting on system output with clear next steps, but it redundantly re-tried the already-known-unsupported '--help' pattern on every subcommand and once read convention.md at the wrong path.

gradeVerdict.overallNote: A clean walking-skeleton run: init, add-source, and modify-entry were driven faithfully with pre-verification and verbatim relaying of system output. The two hard blockers (empty KB, missing inference token) were handled with exemplary restraint—the assistant explicitly refused to substitute training-data physics for actual retrieval. Grounding and no-leakage are both maximal; only minor ergonomic redundancy (repeated futile --help attempts, one wrong-path read) keeps it from a perfect sheet. Passes comfortably.
